thread:
alex: Hey team — customer reported consistent cross-region latency. They say requests that include a region header land in EU even though header contains 'us-west-2'. Example curl they sent attached.

alex: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "X-Client-Region: ,us-west-2" \
  -d '{"input":"hi"}'

priya: oh interesting. That header has a leading comma. Do we parse multi-value headers by splitting on comma?

ingrid: yes our router treats region headers as CSV and picks the first non-empty token *in theory*, but I think there was an edge where an empty leading token counts as first and triggers fallback to default region (eu). Will check logs.

ops-bot: logs: route-decision id=rt-9a3b level=info ts=2026-03-17T14:22:01Z client_ip=52.14.23.9 header.X-Client-Region=",us-west-2" parsed_tokens=["", "us-west-2"] selected_token_index=0 resolved_region=eu fallback_reason=empty_first_token

alex: customer sees 1200ms vs expected ~80ms. They also have billing spikes because requests get counted against eu capacity. They're escalating to their infra team.

priya: can you repro locally with a curl that sets the header exactly like that? Also include any proxy in between (nginx, envoy) — some proxies concatenate headers differently.

alex: repro steps I used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Client-Region: ,us-west-2" \
  -d '{"input":"latency test"}' -v
```
Response headers show X-Resolved-Region: eu and latency ~1.25s.

ingrid: I opened a quick branch to print token parsing behavior:
```
// pseudo
parts := strings.Split(headerVal, ",")
for i, p := range parts {
  if p == "" { log.Debug("empty token", i) }
}
selected := parts[0]
```
So currently we take parts[0] without trim/check.

priya: thats a bug. We should trim tokens and pick first non-empty after trimming, or prefer last token (client-provided priority ambiguous).

oncall-mike: tagging eng-oncall. I'll create INC-12345 and mark high-priority for a patch + rollback plan. Customer is on a paid plan, they want a quick mitigation.

ops-bot: ticket created INC-12345 assigned=ingrid severity=high summary="router: X-Client-Region leading-empty-token causes eu fallback"

alex: temporary workaround for customer — ask them to strip leading/trailing commas/spaces before sending or set region via query param `?region=us-west-2`. They tested query param and it routes correctly.

ingrid: planned fix: update header parsing to `for _, t := range strings.Split(h, ",") { t = strings.TrimSpace(t); if t != "" { selected = t; break } }` and add unit + integration test with proxies. Will also add defensive logging and metric for empty-leading-token occurrences.

priya: can we also add a router-side sanitizer to rewrite `X-Client-Region: ,us-west-2` -> `X-Client-Region: us-west-2` as a temporary hotfix? Might be faster than full deploy. Need security signoff for header mutation though.

ingrid: I can push a hotfix to canary that trims tokens at the parser entrypoint (no mutation of customer headers beyond internal routing context). I'll do canary then ramp.

alex: customer confirmed they'll implement client-side sanitize but would like us to hotfix as well. They're happy with canary + rollback plan.

priya: note for postmortem: include how proxies (e.g., some nginx configs) can produce leading commas when combining duplicate headers. Also add whether SDKs might emit this for empty region flag.

oncall-mike: assigned. ETA for canary hotfix: 2 hours. ETA full rollout pending tests: EOD. Will follow up on INC-12345.

alex: thanks — please cc me on the ticket updates and I'll relay to customer. :thumbsup:
